sections.title: Bytes enter through a format probe
sections.prose: The new_memory_face entry point takes the caller’s data as a byte slice and passes it, with face index and point size, to memory_face; success wraps the parsed Font in a Face, while unsupported or malformed data, an invalid index, or unparseable required tables are documented FontError cases. Before treating the input as TrueType, memory_face probes signatures and text shape for PCF, PFR, WinFNT, BDF, and CID Type 1, immediately dispatching to each matching constructor; the BDF route can return its constructor error before opening a face. If those probes do not select a format, truetype_face is tried; only after its failure and when the input is at least 118 bytes does standalone WinFNT parsing get a chance. A WinFNT unknown-format error replaces the earlier parser error only when the header shape matches; otherwise the original TrueType error survives.

sections.title: SFNT tables become a hinted outline
sections.prose: The TrueType table loader copies loca and glyf bytes into loca_data and glyf_data; either table may be absent only when CFF, CFF2, or sbix supplies another image route, otherwise opening fails. fpgm, prep, and cvt are optional parsed bytecode tables. For a selected glyf range, a zero-length record becomes an empty outline and a record shorter than its 10-byte header is InvalidOutline. When num_contours is nonnegative, the parser reads a simple glyph; the guarded location lookup also distinguishes a bad public glyph index from a bad composite component. A composite glyph instead decodes its component list and recursively invokes load_glyph_inner for each subglyph, then transforms and appends those child points into the parent outline. Before route selection, normalize_load_flags forces NO_SCALE at zero ppem or for NO_RECURSE; NO_SCALE also forces NO_HINTING and NO_BITMAP and removes LoadFlags::RENDER. The ordered LoadFlags branches give FORCE_AUTOHINT its own path only when NO_AUTOHINT is absent, then handle light, no-auto, or default loading; in the scaler, outline_raw comes from an unhinted outline for no-bytecode or auto-hinter cases and from the regular outline loader otherwise. On the native-bytecode route the scaler passes outline_raw.instructions and its prepared context to hint_glyph, which adds four phantom points for bearings and advances. ctx.run_program executes only for nonempty glyph_ins; an interpreter error returns only when pedantic_hinting is set, otherwise the partially interpreted point zone continues.

sections.title: The outline becomes bitmap coverage
sections.prose: A loaded outline is taken for rendering only when render_requested is true; otherwise it remains available in the slot for a later render call. When requested, the transformed outline and selected mode go to render_loaded_outline, and the returned bitmap is installed with set_rendered_bitmap. Before the scalable outline route, svg_allowed lets a found SVG document return an SVG slot instead of a bitmap. If that lookup fails—or SVG is disallowed—svg_only turns the miss into InvalidArgument rather than continuing. An embedded strike is tried only when sbit_allowed, which is false for NO_SCALE or for NO_BITMAP on a scalable face; a successful image returns a bitmap slot before outline loading. An ordinary miss falls through, but sbits_only turns the miss into InvalidArgument, while BITMAP_METRICS_ONLY suppresses the bitmap bytes. render_loaded_outline keeps empty outlines in a special empty-bitmap path for non-normal modes; otherwise RenderMode selects normal gray, monochrome, horizontal or vertical LCD, or SDF conversion. For normal gray rendering, render_normal returns an empty bitmap for no points or contours, reports RasterOverflow for unsafe bounds, and returns a zero-sized bitmap when the pixel box has no area. Otherwise it allocates width×height bytes and calls rasterize; that rasterizer flattens curves, accumulates DDA cells, and sweeps them into 8-bit coverage, with overlapping outlines using rasterize_shifted_in_box_to_with_scratch in a separate branch.

if outline.flags & OUTLINE_OVERLAP != 0 {
        return render_normal_overlap(outline, left, top, width, height, scratch);
    }

    let mut target = vec![0u8; width * height];
    crate::grays::rasterize_shifted_in_box_to_with_scratch(
        &outline,
        0,
        0,
        width,
        height,
        &mut target,
        width,
        1,
        0,
        outline.cbox_x_min,
        outline.cbox_x_max,
        outline.cbox_y_min,
        outline.cbox_y_max,
        scratch,
    )?;
    Ok(RenderedBitmap {
        width: u32_from_usize(width),
        rows: u32_from_usize(height),
        pitch: i32_from_usize(width),
        pixel_mode: PixelMode::Gray,
        num_grays: PixelMode::Gray.num_grays(),
        left,
        top,
        buffer: target,
    })
}
